function.description: Zoom in on a specific region of an image by cropping it based on a bounding box (bbox) and an optional object label
function.name: image_zoom_in_tool

bbox_2d.description: The bounding box of the region to zoom in, as [x1, y1, x2, y2], where (x1, y1) is the top-left corner and (x2, y2) is the bottom-right corner

img_idx.description: The index of the zoomed-in image (starting from 0)

label.description: The name or label of the object in the specified bounding box

function.description: Rotate an image counterclockwise by the given angle in degrees; the canvas is expanded so nothing is cropped
function.name: image_rotate_tool

angle.description: Counterclockwise rotation angle in degrees, e.g. 90, 180, -45

img_idx.description: The index of the image to operate on (starting from 0)

function.description: Mirror an image horizontally (left-right) or vertically (top-bottom)
function.name: image_flip_tool

img_idx.description: The index of the image to operate on (starting from 0)

function.description: Draw auxiliary marks (straight lines, rectangles, points) on a copy of an image, e.g. a horizontal guide line to compare heights or a box around a region
function.name: image_draw_tool

boxes.description: Rectangles as [x1, y1, x2, y2] in pixel coordinates of that image as you see it

function.description: Evaluate an arithmetic expression and return the result (floats shown with 12 significant digits; comparisons, floor/ceil/trunc, // and % use the value as shown). Supports + - * / // % ** (or ^), parentheses, comparisons, lists like [1, 2, 3], the constants pi, e, tau, and the functions abs, acos, acosd, asin, asind, atan, atan2, atan2d, atand, cbrt, ceil, comb, cos, cosd, degrees, exp, factorial, floor, gcd, hypot, lcm, ln, log, log10, log2, max, mean, median, min, perm, pow, pstdev, radians, round, sin, sind, sqrt, stdev, sum, tan, tand, trunc. Write every multiplication with * (2*pi, not 2pi) and call functions by name (sqrt(2), not math.sqrt(2)). % is the remainder, not percent. log and ln are natural logs. sin/cos/tan use radians; sind/cosd/tand/asind/acosd/atand/atan2d use degrees and are exact at special angles. round is Python's round: exact ties go to the even digit.
function.name: calculator

expression.description: The expression to evaluate, e.g. "(12.5 + 7) * 3" or "sqrt(3**2 + 4**2)"

function.description: Read the text in an image (or in one region of it) with an OCR engine. Returns each detected text line with its bounding box [x1, y1, x2, y2] in pixel coordinates of that image as you see it
